newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Restructuring brings profits at Nigeria paint firm.
newsitem.headline: Restructuring brings profits at Nigeria paint firm.

text.p: A management restructuring introduced by Nigerian paints maker IPWA last year has led to profits for the first time in two years, company officials said on Thursday.
They said the company, which last paid a dividend in 1992, posted an after-tax profit of 9.8 million naira by December 31, 1996 compared to a 63.6 million naira loss in the corresponding 1995 period.
Although the company will pay no dividend again this year, it is proposing to increase shareholders' holding by giving one new share for every four, they said.
The company said a rationalising of products and purchase of raw materials at competitive prices were some new measures introduced by its management team.
Brokers at the Nigerian stock exchange said in addition, the company's recovery of its market shares also led to the rise in profits.
IPWA's shares closed steady at 1.81 naira on Thursday.
Industry sources said the country's paints manufacturing sector had been plagued by harsh economic conditions, heavy competition and a low working capital.

Fellow paints makers African Paints published on Wednesday results for the 1996 year ending December 31, which showed it made a 41 million naira loss compared to the 16 million naira profit made in the corresponding 1995 period.
